title: The Hidden Ocean
narration: Beneath a cracked ice shell, an ocean holds twice the water of all Earth's seas. But here, 671,000 kilometers from Jupiter, it stays liquid. How?
visual_goal: A dramatic zoom into Europa's cracked ice surface, then a cutaway revealing a dark, vast ocean below.

title: Jupiter's Grip
narration: Europa is tidally locked, so one side always faces Jupiter. Its orbit is slightly lopsided. Each pass stretches the moon, flexing its interior.
visual_goal: Show Europa orbiting Jupiter with an exaggerated eccentric orbit, flexing and straining.

title: The Heat Engine
narration: That friction generates heat. An eccentricity of 0.009 seems tiny, but it's enough to keep an ocean liquid, 60 to 150 kilometers deep.
visual_goal: Diagram showing tidal flexing generating heat, with an arrow indicating heat rising to the ocean.

title: A Young Surface
narration: This world is geologically alive. Few craters. Long, linear cracks. Scientists say the surface is only 20 to 180 million years old.
visual_goal: Slow pan across Europa's surface, highlighting cracks and ridges with minimal craters.

title: The First Evidence
narration: In 1995, Galileo arrived. For eight years, it orbited Jupiter. Its data pointed to a hidden ocean, changing everything.
visual_goal: Historic footage of Galileo spacecraft, then a cut to its magnetometer readings showing a induced field.

title: The Clues
narration: Ice, salts, sulfuric acid. Tidal heating. A magnetic field that flickers. All puzzle pieces pointing to a vast, salty ocean.
visual_goal: Montage of Europa's surface composition, tidal flexing, and magnetic field lines, with subtle puzzle-like assembly.

title: The Deep Ocean
narration: More than twice the water of all Earth's oceans. The depth? 60 to 150 kilometers. There, in the dark, could life exist?
visual_goal: A cross-section of Europa showing a deep ocean, with faint bioluminescent specks in the dark.

title: The Clock Ticks
narration: In October 2024, Europa Clipper launched. Its journey takes six years. Arrival at Jupiter? April 2030.
visual_goal: Launch footage of Europa Clipper, then a fast-forward animation of its trajectory to Jupiter.

title: The Arrival
narration: In April 2030, the probe will begin its close flybys. Peering through the ice, searching for answers.
visual_goal: Europa Clipper flying over Europa's surface, with instruments scanning the ice.

title: The Question
narration: If that ocean has the chemistry, the heat, and the time — 4.6 billion years — could life have found a foothold? [gasp] We are about to find out.
visual_goal: A hopeful image of Europa's surface with a subtle glow from beneath, hinting at life.
